headline: Deferred two zoning items to October 6, 2026, and closed hearing on a fence height variance without a decision.
summary: The board deferred a proposed lot subdivision at 146 East Avenue and an appeal of a notice of violation at 281 Pearl Street to the October 6, 2026 meeting. The board also heard testimony on a variance request for a six-foot-tall fence at 228 North Winooski Avenue, then closed the hearing to deliberate without recording a final decision.
decisions: Deferred ZP-26-387 at 146 East Avenue to the October 6, 2026 DRB meeting, vote 5-0.
Deferred ZAP-26-12 at 281 Pearl Street to the October 6, 2026 DRB meeting, vote 5-0.

BURLINGTON DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 
Tuesday, September 15, 2026, 5:00 PM 
 
MINUTES 
 
 Hybrid & In Person (at 645 Pine Street) Meeting 
 
Board Members Present: Caitlin Halpert, Evan Gould, Sean McKenzie, Miles Waite, Chase Taylor, and 
Marina Loughlin (5:05 PM) 
 
Board Members Absent: Geoff Hand 
 
Staff Members Present: Mary O’Neil, Kirk Dressing, and Joseph Cava 
 
Staff Members Absent: Scott Gustin and Matthew Clark 
 
I. Agenda 
II. Communications 
III. Minutes 
IV. Public Hearing 
 
1. ZP-26-387; 146 East Avenue (RL, Ward 1) FMB East Avenue, LLC / Taylor Baker   
Proposed subdivision of existing residential lot to create a new 55’ x 167’ residential lot for the 
construction of a new single-family residence. Existing triplex to remain. (Project Manager, Kirk 
Dressing) 
 
Caitlin Halpert: This item has been recommended for deferral to the 10/6/26 DRB meeting. Are 
there any questions or comments from members of the Board or members of the public in attendance 
in person or online? Hearing none, would someone like to make a motion?  
 
Miles Waite: Motioned to defer to the 10/6/26 DRB meeting, Chase Taylor 2nd. Vote 5-0. Motion 
carried.  
 
2. ZAP-26-12; 281 Pearl Street (RH, Ward 8) Sisters & Brothers Investment Group, LLP / Matt 
Handy 
Appeal of issuance of Notice of Violation (NOV) under ZCPT-26-38. (Project Manager, Matthew 
Clark)  
 
Caitlin Halpert: This item has been recommended for deferral to the 10/6/26 DRB meeting. Are 
there any questions or comments from members of the Board or members of the public in attendance 
in person or online? Hearing none, would someone like to make a motion?  
 
Chase Taylor: Motioned to defer to the 10/6/26 DRB meeting, Miles Waite 2nd. Vote 5-0. Motion 
carried.
3. ZP-26-410; 228 North Winooski Avenue (NMU, Ward 2) Champlain Housing Trust / Donal 
Dugan 
Variance request for exemption from maximum allowable fence height to install a six-foot-tall fence 
along the sidewalk to prevent afterhours access to the property. (Project Manager, Kirk Dressing) 
Donal Dugan, Paul Dragon, Amy Demetrowitz, George Harrington, Melo Grant, and Ben Bosley: 
Sworn in. 
 
Caitlin Halpert: Can you tell us about this project? 
 
Donal Dugan: We have been under construction on this site for the past couple of years. We are 
wrapping up with our scheduled construction work. We have been experiencing security issues 
including the accumulation of homeless encampments. We are seeking a variance to have a fence 
taller than the three-foot-tall limit.  
 
Paul Dragon: We are requesting the fence to limit the homelessness issues occurring after operating 
hours. We estimate that there are over three hundred individuals experiencing homelessness in the 
City of Burlington. This has led to an increase in the number of individuals experiencing 
homelessness that are utilizing our services. There needs to be increased communications amongst 
neighbors, tenants, and area business. Through this, we would like to reduce the number of 
complaints and expand this critical community resource. This is a proactive step forward.  
 
Amy Demetrowitz: I have nothing else is add about the relationship of the site. This is a critical 
service to the community. 
 
Caitlin Halpert: It is difficult to grant a variance on fence height and we recognize that this is a 
reoccurring issue.   
 
Donal Dugan: What height can we get that will help to control the site? 
 
Miles Waite: We have had several requests to allow six-foot-tall fencing in the first lot layer of 
properties.  
 
George Harrington: Was there already a six-foot-tall fence in place here before this?   
 
Donal Dugan: A six-foot-tall construction fence was in place here for at least a year. The gates for 
the site is opened up in the morning. It is hard to balance the reality of what currently exists. 
 
Caitlin Halpert: Have you considered other proposals? 
 
Donal Dugan: We did, but it would not work. Where is the restricted site line? The building 
overhangs nears the edge of the street. 
 
Miles Waite: What are you seeking a variance on, height or location? 
 
Donal Dugan: Both.  
 
Sean McKenzie: Have you considered a shorter rolling gate? 
 
Donal Dugan: We did a design that included parking spots outside the fence, but the reality of 
unattended land like parking spots would still cause issues.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? 
Hearing none, are there any questions or comments from members of the public in attendance in 
person or online?
George Harrington: Bad things are happening without prevention in place.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: So you are in favor of a fence? 
 
George Harrington: Yes, it should abut and encompass surrounding properties as well. The fence as 
presented would leave a two-foot gap between the existing property and mine.  
 
Miles Waite: Is traffic one way? It appears there is only one sight line of concern on the corner.  
 
Amy Demetrowitz: There is a column on the edge of the building supporting the corner of the 
overhang.  
 
Kirk Dressing: There is a concern about the sight line and pedestrian versus vehicular traffic.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: From a zoning perspective, I do not see how this proposal can be approved as it is 
presented.  
 
Chase Taylor: As long as the gate is not an egress, can this be utilized? 
 
Caitlin Halpert: There is nothing in Burlington’s Comprehensive Development Ordinance (CDO) 
concerning egress.  
 
Donal Dugan: What about an accordion style gate? 
 
Chase Taylor: Where is the gap between properties that was spoken of during public comment? 
 
Donal Dugan: The gate currently extends to the property line for construction. There would need to 
be a fence agreement in place before extending the fence over the property line.  
 
Melo Grant: It is my opinion to the best of my ability as a City Counselor to address community 
safety issues. There have been a number of recurring issues over the past three years. My concerns 
are in regard to the codes of what is allowed and reaching the end goal of resolving a variety of 
issues. I want to plant the seed for changes in regulations.  
 
Evan Gould: The Planning Commission is where these issues should be addressed, not the 
Development Review Board.  
 
Melo Grant: We will see a rise in variance requests because of this issue.  
 
Ben Bosley: Any progress on complex projects such as this should be carefully considered.  
 
Mary O’Neil: I do not believe this is an appropriate forum to address this. This Board addresses 
questions concerning proposed project development, not speculate on future changes.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Hearing no additional questions or comments, we will close the hearing on this item 
to deliberate on this evening’s agenda items.  
 
V. Adjournment 
Hearing closed at 5:40 PM. 
 
 
 
Participation in the DRB proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal.  Please note that ANYTHING 
submitted to the Zoning office is considered public and cannot be kept confidential. This may not be the final order in which items
will be heard. Please view final Agenda, at https://burlingtonvt.portal.civicclerk.com/ or the office notice board, one week before the 
hearing for the order in which items will be heard.
